Working collaboratively with the School of Nursing (SON) course faculty, the Clinical Preceptor facilitates clinical learning experiences developed as part of the nursing curriculum. Through direct supervision, role modeling, and coaching, the Clinical Preceptor supports the development of students' clinical knowledge, technical skills, professional behaviors, clinical judgment, and critical thinking. The Clinical Preceptor promotes a safe, supportive, and engaging learning environment while providing formative and summative feedback regarding student performance using standardized evaluation tools. Example of Duties Qualified candidates with demonstrated clinical expertise are encouraged to apply.Participate in required clinical orientation sessions and educational activities offered by Husson University School of Nursing and the assigned clinical agency. Directly supervise a group of BSN nursing students in the assigned clinical setting in accordance with course learning outcomes, professional standards, and the policies of both the School of Nursing and the clinical agency. Facilitate student learning through clinical teaching, coaching, role modeling, and direct supervision while promoting safe, ethical, evidence-based nursing practice. Conduct pre- and post-clinical conferences using course objectives and learning activities. Provide timely, constructive feedback to students using standardized clinical evaluation tools. Communicate regularly with SON course faculty regarding student progress, concerns, and recommendations for additional support or remediation. Provide the SON course faculty with a summary of each clinical day, including student progress, learning opportunities, and any significant issues or concerns. Contribute objective performance feedback for midterm and final student evaluations using standardized evaluation criteria. Notify the SON course faculty promptly of student absences, injuries, illnesses, safety concerns, or professional conduct issues occurring during the clinical experience. Collaborate with SON course faculty to promote consistent clinical instruction and student success. Qualifications Current, active, and unrestricted Registered Nurse (RN) license in the State of Maine. Bachelor's degree in Nursing (BSN) required; Master's degree in Nursing (MSN) preferred. Specialty certification relevant to the clinical area is desirable. Minimum of one (1) year of active clinical nursing experience required; three (3) or more years of active clinical practice preferred. jobs.description: Allocation of Faculty Resources The Academic Affairs Council (AAC) is tasked with the judicious allocation of resources that support the academic mission of Bates College. This work takes many forms, but includes allotting tenure-track and nontenure-track faculty positions to academic units and deciding which units will have access to replacement or additional courses in a particular academic year. For Tenure track faculty positions, each fall, the AAC issues a call for position concepts detailing the process for applying for faculty resources and / or reauthorizations. Data Used by the AAC The TPT is an online “dashboard” that helps faculty think about workload in their program or department. The data in the TPT will be refreshed by September 1 each year. Enrollment and Majors data for the academic units at the college is available from this report. The AAC uses these data along with other information to make resource allocation decisions. You must be on campus or connected to the campus computer network to view the report. Like the TPT, the data will be refreshed by September 1 of each year. The Three Year Plan For allocating temporary faculty resources such as visiting faculty or course replacements, the AAC has asked all chairs to include the details of such requests in the three-year plan they complete and submit annually. Download a blank 3YP form The 3YP is a spreadsheet that helps the AAC do academic planning. It has a set of tabs that program and department chairs can use to forecast personnel needs for their academic unit over the next three years. It is designed to combine information about leaves, course releases, additional courses, replacement courses, and retirements in one place. This process does NOT replace the faculty line/lectureship proposal process (if you plan to participate in that), although information about anticipated proposals is requested to be included in the 3YP on the Line Request tab. Each chair must complete a 3-year plan by October 7 each year. If you have questions about how to fill it out, please contact Matt Duvall (mduvall@bates.edu). jobs.description: Career opportunities at COA Work at College of the Atlantic Join a small, collaborative community on the Maine coast College of the Atlantic (COA) is an equal opportunity employer and is committed to fostering learning and working environments free from discrimination. The college adheres to all applicable state and federal equal opportunity laws and regulations. In employment, admissions, and access to our educational programs, COA does not discriminate on the basis of age, race, color, sex or gender (including gender identity and expression), pregnancy, sexual orientation, religion, religious practices, mental or physical disability, genetic predisposition, national or ethnic origin, citizenship status, veteran status, marital or partnership status, or any other legally protected status. faculty Position Overview College of the Atlantic seeks a full-time faculty member in agroecology who is actively interested in teaching and collaborating across disciplinary boundaries. We seek a practicing agroecologist with a strong foundation in plant and soil sciences, interdisciplinary research interests, and a strong commitment to teaching and mentoring students within COA’s single undergraduate degree in human ecology. Candidates at any career stage are welcome. A PhD in agroecology, agronomy, botany, soil science, ecology, or a related field is required by the anticipated start date (September 1, 2027). This is a full‑time (10-month), permanent, benefits eligible position. The successful candidate will be an engaged scholar-practitioner who approaches agroecology as science, practice, and social movement. They will contribute to COA’s experiential, place-based pedagogy and interdisciplinary curriculum. Teaching responsibilities include undergraduate courses in food and farming systems—such as agroecosystems, soil ecology, seed systems, and organic farming and gardening—as well as contributing to the introductory biology and ecology curriculum. The teaching load is five courses across three 10-week trimesters (e.g., 1-2-2). Other responsibilities include mentoring and advising students, supervising senior capstone projects and independent studies, and contributing to college governance. COA emphasizes experiential learning. The successful candidate will engage students through the college’s two organic farms, greenhouses, and community garden, using these as living laboratories for teaching and research. They will provide meaningful opportunities for students to engage in field-based inquiry and research, with possible areas of inquiry including agroecology and social movements, agroecosystem design, agroecology in urban contexts, climate change adaptation, and participatory or farmer-centered research. All COA students design individualized, interdisciplinary degrees within our Bachelor of Arts in Human Ecology. Some students go on to graduate studies in food systems or closely aligned fields; others use their academic training in food systems to prepare for work on farms as growers and land stewards; in government, nonprofit, and policy roles advancing food access and sustainable agriculture and fisheries; and in politics and activism shaping food systems transformation. Others start or support values-driven food businesses, or bring agroecological perspectives into education, the arts, and community organizing. Successful candidates for this position will have experience working with diverse student populations and demonstrate strong potential for innovative teaching and transdisciplinary collaboration.
